capabilities: Draw a graph where tags, folders and note properties act as hub nodes
Tag notes, set properties, merge and rename tags by dragging or right-clicking
Show a details panel with usage counts, folders, co-occurring values and look-alike tags
Hide rarely used values and split tag hubs by folder
Use Bases filters and the standard graph controls to scope what is drawn
extras: Makes no network requests and works on desktop and mobile. After an update, a one-time message asks users to star the GitHub repository. Built for bases of up to a few thousand notes; undo covers only the last edit.
intentEvidence: It is a Bases view: the base's filters decide what is drawn.
motivation: The author collected still-open graph and tag feature requests from six months of Obsidian forum threads and built the plugin to answer them.
problem: Obsidian's graph view is read-only and shows only links, so notes held together by tags or properties have no visual structure and tagging or merging tags means editing each note by hand.

relations.evidence: The gear button in the graph's toolbar opens the controls you know from Obsidian's own graph view

summary: A graph view for Bases where tags, folders and properties become hub nodes, and dragging lets you tag, merge and reorganize notes.
